purpose: Test whether the Magnicon XXF-1 10 kHz response can remain second order while a non-Bessel damping/Q removes the residual, with c2 fixed to zero and the same relaxed thermal-backbone profile.

magnicon_filter.manual_statement: Connector-box anti-alias filters are second-order Bessel, cutoff 10 kHz +/-2.5%.
magnicon_filter.semantics: For the documented phase-normalized 2nd-order Bessel, the natural denominator frequency equals the 10 kHz nominal cutoff and Q=1/sqrt(3). The free-Q branch keeps a two-pole denominator and profiles only its damping Q; once Q is non-Bessel, the 9.75-10.25 kHz coordinate is treated as the natural frequency f0, not asserted to be a measured -3 dB cutoff.

guardrail: The XXF-1 manual documents a second-order Bessel 10 kHz +/-2.5% output filter. Free Q is a diagnostic deformation of the ideal Bessel transfer, not evidence that the hardware Q differs from 1/sqrt(3). A successful free-Q fit would show only that corner damping/shape can absorb the residual without changing filter order or adding c2.
